points.title: Data dictionary
points.must: A document describing every field of every table: name, data type, size, format, key, validation, description, example — data about the data (metadata).

points.title: Who uses the data dictionary
points.must: Programmers build the tables from it, testers plan test data from the validation column, the client checks the data, maintainers read it later.

points.title: The columns one by one
points.must: What each column records: field name (no spaces, FK named like its PK), type, size, format, key, validation with limits, description, example; each entity of the ERD becomes one table, each attribute one row.

points.title: Data type and choosing it
points.must: Definition; INT, DECIMAL, REAL, CHAR/VARCHAR, DATE/TIME, BOOLEAN — each with an example field and why (phone and IIN as text, money as DECIMAL, dates as DATE).

points.title: Field sizes
points.must: Size fits the longest realistic value, e.g. S0107 → 5, +77015554433 → 12, surname 30; DECIMAL(7,2) for prices.

points.title: A full data dictionary example
points.must: At least one table (e.g. Student, Lesson or Product) written out with name, type, size, key, validation, description and example.

points.title: Foreign keys match primary keys
points.must: An FK must have the same data type and size as the PK it refers to, otherwise the join and referential integrity fail.

points.title: Validation checks
points.must: Definition (reasonable, not correct); presence, type, length, range, format, lookup and uniqueness — each with an example rule with limits.

points.title: Validation vs verification
points.must: Validation = automatic check that data is sensible; verification = check that data matches the source (double entry, visual check) — with an example validation cannot catch.

points.title: Data integrity
points.must: Accuracy and consistency of data; entity integrity (PK), referential integrity (every FK matches an existing PK, with an example), domain integrity (type, size, validation).

points.title: From the dictionary to SQL
points.must: Each row → one field line; PK → PRIMARY KEY; FK → FOREIGN KEY … REFERENCES; presence → NOT NULL; unique → UNIQUE; range → CHECK; DEFAULT; formats in the form.

points.title: CREATE TABLE example and order
points.must: A complete CREATE TABLE for a link table with PK, two FKs, NOT NULL and CHECK/DEFAULT; one-side tables first, link table last.

points.title: The DBMS enforces the design
points.must: The DBMS refuses records that break PK, FK, NOT NULL or CHECK rules (e.g. a lesson for S9999); validate both in the form and in the database.

points.title: Testing and checking the design
points.must: Normal, boundary and erroneous test records; run the queries for every required report; check requirements, 3NF, keys, types and validation.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: At least two: INT for a phone/IIN; REAL for money; dates as text; FK type differs from PK; range check on a name; missing REFERENCES in SQL.
